messages:
maria_support: Customer report — dashboard shows region = EU (eu-west-1) but our access logs show X-Redwood-Serving-Region: us-central-1 for the same requests. They see higher p99 latency (~450ms) and intermittent 401s. Customer says their app pins to eu-west. Can we triage?

tim_ops: Can you paste a sample request_id and the raw request headers from their logs? we can look up routing decisions.

maria_support: sample request_id: req_0a7f9b2c. From edge logs (sanitized):

```
RequestID: req_0a7f9b2c
ClientIP: 35.198.12.99
X-Redwood-Serving-Region: us-central-1
X-Redwood-Region-Label: eu-west-1
Auth: Bearer <redacted>
LatencyMs: 462
Status: 200 / 401 (intermittent)
```

li_engineer: Interesting — console label (X-Redwood-Region-Label) is from our UI routing heuristic (geoip + tenant preference) but the X-Redwood-Serving-Region header is set by the edge that actually forwarded the request. The latter is authoritative for where the request was served.

li_engineer: My hypothesis: eu-west POP dropped below capacity and requests were transparently failing over to us-central (cross-pop failover). Console still shows the tenant's preferred region (eu-west) because we cache the mapping for 5m. That mismatch explains latency. The 401s could be from token verification hitting a different keyset replication lag or from IP-restricted API keys.

sean_sre: FYI we've seen replication lag cause sporadic 401s when LPUs validate tokens against a slightly stale JWKS cache in remote POPs. Repro steps I use:

1) curl to endpoint with tenant API key pinned to eu-west:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" \
  -H "Host: api.redwood.example" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=redwood-1
```
2) inspect response headers for X-Redwood-Serving-Region and X-Redwood-Auth-Source.
3) if served from other POP, check /_internal/jwks-version on that POP.

li_engineer: Quick mitigation options:
- remove the stale console mapping (invalidate tenant region cache) so UI shows "served_from: us-central-1" until routing stabilizes, OR
- set a customer-level route override to prefer eu-west for that tenant (forces sticky routing) while we investigate.

tim_ops: I'm going to open an infra ticket. Also we should confirm whether billing headers used for invoice-region attribution are using console label or the served-from header — that could affect their invoice.

deploy-bot: canary-rollout:region-routing-fix v2.3.1 started by li_engineer — 3/10 hosts.

li_engineer: opened https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-4821 with traces, sample reqs, and suggested mitigations. I'll watch the canary.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll tell the customer: 1) we see failover to us-central, 2) we're rolling a canary fix that will surface served-from in the console immediately and add a short-term tenant override, 3) we'll follow up on the 401s once SRE confirms JWKS replication status. Will update here when customer responds. :thumbsup:

sean_sre: note: also check any IP-restrictions on the customer's API key (they may have allowed only eu-west IPs). cross-pop serving would break that and cause 401s.

maria_support: good call, pinging customer to double-check allowed IPs.

li_engineer: canary is healthy on 3/3 hosts now, rolling remainder. I'll post result in 10m.

maria_support: ack — leaving thread open for canary results and customer confirmation."
